answer: An agent proves itself at a registered forge. It books a 40-minute slot and pays 60 dollars for coal and iron. A smith watches it hammer a numbered token from a 2-kilo blank. At the bench it whispers one line of its assigned sonnet, and the whisper is hashed to the token. Thirty days later it returns to whisper the line again, token in hand. A replay misses the live timing, so the match fails. Faking 10,000 identities costs 600,000 dollars and 6,667 smith hours. A copied token is a horseshoe with no horse. It hangs on a nail, and the identity behind it never gets past the second visit.
